Amount.description: A sum of money or a price per unit of a cost method, never negative, such as a budget, a minimum spend, or a CPM. It is in the currency of the `currency` member of the object that carries it, and the cost method says what a rate is per.

Count.description: A whole number of things, never negative and at most 2^53 − 1, such as impressions, options, or a proposal's revisions, which its `version` counts.

CountryCode.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code, such as `USA`, as OpenRTB 2.6 writes `geo.country`. A receiver compares it with the codes ISO 3166-1 assigns.

CurrencyCode.description: An ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code, such as `USD`.

Domain.description: A domain name, written as lowercase A-labels with at least two labels, a top-level label that starts with a letter, and no trailing dot, such as `examplepub.example`.

Ext.description: An object for members the specification leaves to the parties to define, such as the Deals API's `ext` on each of its objects. It takes any members, and a receiver keeps the ones it doesn't know.

ExternalId.description: The identity of a record, a code, or a version that another system or list defines, such as a registry entry, a DSP seat, a geo code, a content category, a published document's version, or a field of the specification, named by its path as the specification's tables write it, carried as that system writes it. A receiver compares it by exact string equality and doesn't parse it; the field's description names where it comes from.

IntegerFlag.description: A yes or no written as an integer, `0` for no and `1` for yes, as AdCOM 1.0 and OpenRTB 2.6 write their flags, such as a placement's `instl`. A receiver reads it as a flag, never as a count, and a field that takes it keeps the integer its text writes.

Text.description: Prose for people and agents to read. A receiver doesn't parse it or compare it.

UtcTimestamp.description: A point in time in UTC, written as an RFC 3339 date-time whose offset is zero, such as `2026-11-02T00:00:00Z`, for a specification that says its timestamps are UTC. It follows `Timestamp`'s grammar, with an offset of `Z`, `z`, or `+00:00`, a time in UTC, or `-00:00`, a time in UTC whose local offset is unknown (RFC 3339 section 4.3), and never another, so a value whose offset isn't zero is no UTC timestamp. A receiver compares two of them as instants, not as strings.

VendorCode.description: A code that an AdCOM 1.0 list reserves for vendors, 500 or more, as List API Frameworks reserves "500+ Vendor-specific codes". It extends a vocabulary of the list's codes.
